scenes.tts: Does a signal from the axon tip really keep the cell body alive? And what actually makes the trip?
scenes.visual: Title card: Courier or Relay? A neuron with a long axon, terminals at right.
scenes.narration: Does a signal from the axon tip really keep the cell body alive? And what actually makes the trip?

scenes.tts: First, radioactive N G F placed in a target built up in the matching ganglion on the same side. In the chick, the motor neurons beside it stayed unlabelled.
scenes.caption: First, radioactive NGF placed in a target built up in the matching ganglion on the same side. In the chick, the motor neurons beside it stayed unlabelled.
scenes.visual: Left: label from the eye builds up in the same-side superior cervical ganglion. Right: a chick embryo, label from the leg in same-side sensory ganglia; the motor column beside them stays dark.
scenes.narration: First, radioactive NGF placed in a target built up in the matching ganglion on the same side. In the chick, the motor neurons beside it stayed unlabelled.

scenes.tts: But label shows only where radioactivity went, not whether it mattered for survival.
scenes.visual: Three question marks beside the labelled ganglion: intact? active? survival?
scenes.narration: But label shows only where radioactivity went, not whether it mattered for survival.

scenes.tts: Robert Campenot's dish answered that. Sealed dividers split it into chambers whose fluids do not mix.
scenes.visual: Top view of the compartmented dish: a centre chamber and side chambers separated by sealed dividers.
scenes.narration: Robert Campenot's dish answered that. Sealed dividers split it into chambers whose fluids do not mix.

scenes.tts: Cell bodies sit in the centre. Their axons grow under the seal into side chambers.
scenes.visual: Rat sympathetic neurons in the centre; axons pass under the seal into a side chamber.
scenes.narration: Cell bodies sit in the centre. Their axons grow under the seal into side chambers.

scenes.tts: Give the cell bodies no N G F. Let their axons reach a chamber that has it. Do the cell bodies live?
scenes.caption: Give the cell bodies no NGF. Let their axons reach a chamber that has it. Do the cell bodies live?
scenes.visual: Centre chamber labelled no NGF; one side chamber labelled NGF. A question mark over the cell bodies.
scenes.narration: Give the cell bodies no NGF. Let their axons reach a chamber that has it. Do the cell bodies live?

scenes.tts: Many survive. A signal from the distal axons, the far ends near the terminals, can keep the cell body alive.
scenes.visual: The cell bodies stay bright. Label: distal axons, the far ends near the terminals.
scenes.narration: Many survive. A signal from the distal axons, the far ends near the terminals, can keep the cell body alive.

scenes.tts: With N G F only on distal axons, Kreb became phosphorylated in the nuclei. Kreb is a transcription factor that switches genes on.
scenes.caption: With NGF only on distal axons, CREB became phosphorylated in the nuclei. CREB is a transcription factor that switches genes on.
scenes.visual: Credit: Riccio and colleagues, Ginty laboratory. NGF in the side chamber only; the nuclei light up. Label: phosphorylated CREB.
scenes.narration: With NGF only on distal axons, CREB became phosphorylated in the nuclei. CREB is a transcription factor that switches genes on.

scenes.tts: That needed Track A kinase activity in the cell body. But was that the same receptor, carried from the tip?
scenes.caption: That needed TrkA kinase activity in the cell body. But was that the same receptor, carried from the tip?
scenes.visual: TrkA lit in the cell body. Label: TrkA kinase needed in the cell body. A question mark: carried from the tip?
scenes.narration: That needed TrkA kinase activity in the cell body. But was that the same receptor, carried from the tip?

scenes.tts: So how did it travel? Courier. The N G F and Track A complex itself is carried the whole way.
scenes.caption: So how did it travel? Courier. The NGF and TrkA complex itself is carried the whole way.
scenes.visual: Top drawing: one endosome rides from tip to cell body and lights up on arrival. Label: courier.
scenes.narration: So how did it travel? Courier. The NGF and TrkA complex itself is carried the whole way.

scenes.tts: Relay. Each stretch of axon switches on the next, like a row of dominoes. No one molecule makes the whole trip.
scenes.visual: Bottom drawing: segments light up one after another, and nothing moves between them. Label: relay.
scenes.narration: Relay. Each stretch of axon switches on the next, like a row of dominoes. No one molecule makes the whole trip.

scenes.tts: Blocking dynein stops survival. Does that prove a courier?
scenes.visual: Both drawings: dynein marked with a block symbol. Credit: Heerssen and colleagues, 2004.
scenes.narration: Blocking dynein stops survival. Does that prove a courier?

scenes.tts: No. If each relay step needed dynein, the relay would stop too. This block cannot tell them apart.
scenes.visual: Both drawings go dark together. Label: this block cannot tell them apart.
scenes.narration: No. If each relay step needed dynein, the relay would stop too. This block cannot tell them apart.

scenes.tts: So block Track A's kinase only in the middle stretch, with an inhibitor applied only there. What does each model predict?
scenes.caption: So block TrkA's kinase only in the middle stretch, with an inhibitor applied only there. What does each model predict?
scenes.visual: A three-segment axon; the middle segment greyed out, labelled TrkA kinase inhibitor, this stretch only. Note: a courier test needs transport to keep running. Credit: Ye, Kuruvilla, Zweifel and Ginty, 2003.
scenes.narration: So block TrkA's kinase only in the middle stretch, with an inhibitor applied only there. What does each model predict?

scenes.tts: A relay that needs Track A kinase in each stretch would break at the gap. A carried complex could pass through and signal again.
scenes.visual: Relay drawing: the signal stops at the grey segment. Courier drawing: the endosome dims while crossing the grey segment, then lights up again in the cell body.
scenes.narration: A relay that needs TrkA kinase in each stretch would break at the gap. A carried complex could pass through and signal again.
scenes.caption: A relay that needs TrkA kinase in each stretch would break at the gap. A carried complex could pass through and signal again.

scenes.tts: The signal still reached the cell bodies, and the neurons survived. N G F also had to be taken into the cell.
scenes.caption: The signal still reached the cell bodies, and the neurons survived. NGF also had to be taken into the cell.
scenes.visual: The cell bodies stay bright. Label: evidence against a TrkA-kinase relay; supports a courier. Inset: labelled endosomes moving back along an axon (Heerssen and colleagues; Cui and colleagues, 2007).
scenes.narration: The signal still reached the cell bodies, and the neurons survived. NGF also had to be taken into the cell.

scenes.tts: Two results keep the question open. Track A in the cell bodies was phosphorylated within a minute, far faster than endosomes move.
scenes.visual: On screen: TrkA phosphorylated in cell bodies within 1 minute. Far faster than dynein-driven endosomes move.
scenes.narration: Two results keep the question open. TrkA in the cell bodies was phosphorylated within a minute, far faster than endosomes move.
scenes.caption: Two results keep the question open. TrkA in the cell bodies was phosphorylated within a minute, far faster than endosomes move.

scenes.tts: And N G F fixed to beads supported survival with little or no N G F transport.
scenes.caption: And NGF fixed to beads supported survival with little or no NGF transport.
scenes.visual: NGF on beads stays at the axon tips; the cell bodies stay bright. Label: little or no NGF transport detected. A faint dotted path toward the cell bodies marks what the assay could miss.
scenes.narration: And NGF fixed to beads supported survival with little or no NGF transport.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: for survival, the evidence favours a courier. Whether a faster signal also helps is still open.
scenes.visual: Closing card: courier favoured, for survival. A faster signal: open.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: for survival, the evidence favours a courier. Whether a faster signal also helps is still open.
